subject: literature
passage: Birgitta had not seen the farmhouse in thirty years, and she drove out to the auction intending only to watch it sold. She had no use, she told herself, for a cold stone house. Yet as the bidding began, she found herself noticing the elm her father had planted the year she was born, and the kitchen window from which her mother used to call her in at dusk. When the auctioneer paused, her hand was already in the air. Driving home, she could not have said when she had decided to bid, only that leaving the house to strangers had turned out to be impossible.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Birgitta decides to buy the farmhouse so that she can replant the garden her father began.
choices.B: Birgitta, who meant only to watch the farmhouse sold, is moved by her memories to buy it.
choices.C: Birgitta regrets bidding on a farmhouse that she knows she will never be able to use.
choices.D: Birgitta attends the auction because she wants to make sure the farmhouse is sold to a good family.

explanation.why: The text sets up Birgitta's intention "only to watch" and her belief that she has "no use" for the house. Her memories of the elm and the kitchen window change her mind, and she bids almost without deciding to. The main idea is the shift from detachment to an emotional purchase.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The elm her father planted is one of her memories, but the text says nothing about replanting a garden.
explanation.B: Correct. This covers her original intention, the memories that move her, and the bid that follows.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not express regret; it says leaving the house to strangers was "impossible."
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says she came only to watch and makes no mention of other buyers' suitability.
